Task 3.2.2: Kraken Mare Implementation – “Full” A more complete demonstration of the Kraken Mare (KM) data infrastructure will be performed using a more complete list of metrics agreed upon by NREL and HPE. HPE and NREL will transform a jointly identified set of existing sensors gathered from the building management system, CRC, CDUs, etc. to KM format. HPE and NREL to decide upon which sensors to use. At a minimum the metrics used to calculate PUE and those required for Tasks 3-6 will be transformed. 5 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. NREL deliverables: • Use platform provided in Task 1 to host KM components. • Ensure that all metrics (of interest) are streaming and available on Kafka. HPE to work with NREL to identify key metrics. • Participate in learning sensor behavior and updating sensor metadata. Use HPE provided tool to initially characterize sensors. • Help quantify the value of KM to learn and characterize sensors. Provide feedback on the design, implementation, and value of KM in NREL’s production environment. HPE deliverables: • Provide tools to simplify the task of characterizing sensors. • Provide KM containers/orchestration for Framework Manager (which holds the sensor metadata). • Work with NREL to identify required metrics not yet collected on the system, such as CoolingRack and CDU metrics, and building metrics (as necessary), and develop mechanisms to collect this data and store it in the NREL Elasticsearch database. Task 3.2.3: Anomaly Detection - Single Metrics • In Year 1, significant progress was made towards single metric anomaly detection using Machine Learning (statistical) techniques. This effort will continue in Year 2. • NREL deliverables: • NREL to label a subset of metrics for HPE, with a focus on anomalies that are easy to detect. • NREL to work with HPE to identify a set of metrics for which it is possible to build models of anomalies. These models will be used to generate synthetic anomalies to evaluate anomaly detection pipelines and select the most suitable configuration for each given metric automatically. Focus will be on anomaly models for single metrics. • NREL to provide both data science feedback on the algorithms as well as operational effectiveness of the associated results after HPE has run anomaly detection algorithm(s) on labelled data. • NREL and HPE to iterate algorithm detection performance until algorithms are performing acceptably. HPE deliverables: • HPE to create an anomaly detection evaluation pipeline and create documentation and code to evaluate anomaly detection pipelines in supervised and unsupervised regimes. • HPE to create pre-configured anomaly detection pipelines for a selected set of metrics that are evaluated and tested in an isolated environment (i.e., without integration with tools such as HPCM). 6 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications.
